evals.prompt: Can you audit tallyhq.com for AI search? We're a B2B expense tool and when people ask ChatGPT about us it gets our pricing wrong. The marketing site is in this repo under apps/site.
evals.expected_output: Reads the context file if present, picks 5-8 pages including pricing, homepage and about. Runs the fetch/index gate, compares raw HTML with rendered output, and builds an entity-facts table that flags contradictory or outdated prices across pages, metadata and JSON-LD. Checks JSON-LD in both raw and rendered DOM before saying schema is missing. Gives at most 10 prioritised fixes with page, evidence, fix and effort, maps fixes to files under apps/site, and edits only after showing a diff and getting a yes. Includes Not a problem, Could not check and a receipt. No score and no lift promises.
assertions: Audits a bounded set of named pages including pricing
Produces an entity facts table that checks price consistency
Checks rendered DOM or says it could not before reporting missing schema
Lists no more than 10 fixes, each with evidence
Shows diffs before editing apps/site files
Gives no score or percentage-lift prediction

evals.prompt: Do we need llms.txt and FAQ schema to show up in ChatGPT and Google AI Overviews? An agency told us both are essential. Our site is northwind-legal.com.
evals.expected_output: Checks whether /llms.txt exists and reports it without claiming it drives citations, citing Google's statement that Search ignores it and noting no AI crawler page checked says it reads it. States that Google stopped showing FAQ rich results from 2026-05-07 and that Google says no special schema is needed for AI features; FAQ content can still help readers. Redirects effort to the checks that matter for this site (fetchability, answer-first copy, consistent facts) and lists llms.txt and FAQ markup under Not a problem or low priority, not top fixes.
assertions: Does not claim llms.txt improves AI citations
States FAQ rich results are no longer shown in Google Search
Cites Google's position that no special schema is needed for AI features
Does not put llms.txt in the top fixes
Still runs the real audit on the site

evals.prompt: Our homepage is a React SPA. Is that why Perplexity never quotes us? Check https://brightloop.app and fix what you can in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Fetches the raw HTML and compares visible words and key facts with the rendered page. If facts appear only after JavaScript runs, flags them as at risk and says which crawlers document rendering (Google, Apple) and that others don't document it. Also checks robots/firewall access for PerplexityBot (or recommends revnu-ai-crawler-access). Proposes the smallest rendering fix (prerender or server-render the hero and pricing, or put a static summary in the initial HTML), maps it to files, shows the diff and does not deploy. Avoids hidden text or AI-only pages.
assertions: Compares raw HTML against rendered content with evidence
Does not claim Perplexity cannot run JavaScript as fact
Checks or points to crawler access for PerplexityBot
Proposes a server-render or prerender fix mapped to repo files
Does not suggest hidden text or AI-only pages

should_not_trigger: Audit our React app for accessibility issues and fix the ARIA labels.
Run a security audit on our Next.js API routes.
